# Building HTTP Clients

Many modern CLI tools interact with cloud APIs, fetch remote manifests, download binary updates, or query telemetry endpoints. `reqwest` provides both synchronous (blocking) and asynchronous HTTP clients.

## Adding `reqwest` and `serde`

In `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "blocking"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
```

## Synchronous (Blocking) Client for Simple CLIs

For lightweight CLIs that execute a single sequential HTTP request, the blocking client avoids the overhead and runtime setup of a full async event loop:

```rust
use reqwest::blocking::Client;
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::time::Duration;
use anyhow::{Context, Result};

#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
struct ReleaseInfo {
    tag_name: String,
    published_at: String,
}

fn fetch_latest_release(repo: &str) -> Result<ReleaseInfo> {
    let client = Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
        .user_agent("mycli/1.0.0")
        .build()?;

    let url = format!("https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases/latest");
    
    let release = client
        .get(&url)
        .send()
        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to connect to {url}"))?
        .error_for_status()?
        .json::<ReleaseInfo>()?;

    Ok(release)
}
```

## Streaming Downloads with Progress Feedback

When downloading large binary payloads or archives, streaming the response body chunk by chunk prevents excessive memory allocation and enables real-time progress reporting:

```rust
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{copy, BufWriter};
use anyhow::Result;

fn download_file(url: &str, destination: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let mut response = reqwest::blocking::get(url)?;
    let file = File::create(destination)?;
    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(file);

    copy(&mut response, &mut writer)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
